rounds.text: Sonam Ltd demonstrates robust top-line and bottom-line compounding, evidenced by 10-year and 5-year sales growth both sitting at 17% alongside 3-year sales growth accelerating to 27% [E14, E15, E16]. This operational momentum is further validated by a stellar rules-based screen score of 88 out of 100 carrying a medium confidence BUY rating [E61], supported by recent quarterly metrics showing extraordinary year-over-year sales growth of 76% and net profit surges of 127% [E62, E64]. Profitability efficiency also outpaces broader sector benchmarks, with the company delivering a superior ROA of 7.84%, ROE of 10.24%, and ROCE of 13.27% compared to respective sector medians of 4.96%, 8.65%, and 10.27% [E8, E9, E10]. Financial health remains conservative with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.30x [E36], complemented by substantial free cash flow generation of Rs 4 Cr in March 2026 [E35] and a dramatic efficiency gain in debtor days improving from 30.1 down to 17.3 days [E57]. Momentum is extraordinarily strong, reflected by a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E48], a twelve-month price return of 78.4% [E49], and a technical posture where the share price remains comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E47]. Conceded: the company carries an operating margin contraction from 14% down to 8% over the trailing twelve months [E29] and promoter holdings have declined significantly from 72.47% to 57.73% [E39].

Sonam Ltd trades at a significant valuation premium, with a P/E of 34.08x against a sector benchmark of 25.59x [E6] and an EV/EBITDA of 18.8x against a sector benchmark of 14.44x [E11]. This valuation appears disconnected from underlying performance, as price growth has exceeded profit growth by 61% recently [E54], and the stock is currently trading at a P/B of 5.19x against a sector benchmark of 2.02x [E7]. Operational efficiency is under pressure, with operating margins contracting from 14% to 8% over the last three years [E29] while the three-year return on equity remains low at 10.6% [E60]. The sharp decline in promoter holdings from 72.47% to 57.73% suggests a lack of confidence from those closest to the business [E39], especially as holdings decreased further by 0.39% in the last quarter [E59]. Furthermore, the stock's historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -60.3% [E50] and high annualized volatility of 41.3% [E51] highlight the substantial risk for investors at these elevated price levels. Conceded: the company has achieved a 127% year-over-year increase in net profit [E64] and a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of 17% [E14].

Conceded: [E6], [E7], [E11], [E29], [E39], [E50], [E51], [E54], [E59], and [E60]. While the bear highlights multiple valuation and historical risk concerns, the underlying business performance is exceptionally robust, evidenced by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 67% [E17] and a net profit surge of 127% year-over-year [E64]. Operational return metrics tell a superior profitability story, with the company’s return on assets (7.84%), return on equity (10.24%), and return on capital employed (13.27%) all outperforming their respective sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10]. Furthermore, financial health remains conservatively managed with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.30x [E36], backed by positive operating cash flow of Rs 6 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 4 Cr in March 2026 [E34, E35]. Efficiency has also strengthened as debtor days have dramatically improved from 30.1 to 17.3 days [E57]. Finally, the rules-based screen awards the company a strong 88 out of 100 with a medium confidence buy rating [E61], supported by technical momentum where the price sits above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E47] alongside a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E48].

Conceded: [E17], [E34], [E35], [E57], [E61], [E64]. While trailing sales and profit surges are noted, the bull ignores that this momentum is completely detached from a fragile margin profile, evidenced by an operating margin that collapsed by 6 percentage points from historical levels to 8% in the TTM and remains inconsistent [E29, E31, E32]. The reliance on high relative strength and technical moving averages [E47, E48] masks extreme vulnerability, given that the stock sits 95% to 97% of the way up its 52-week range [E5, E45] and carries a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -60.3% [E50]. Furthermore, despite outperforming sector ROCE benchmarks [E10], the company's absolute median return on equity has stagnated at a low 10% to 11% over 3, 5, and 10-year periods [E25, E26, E27], which explicitly triggers a negative flag for low historical returns on equity [E60]. Finally, the touted operational efficiency and cash flows are undermined by rising borrowings, which increased from Rs 18 Cr to Rs 21 Cr in Mar 2026 [E37], alongside a severe insider exodus as promoter holdings plummeted by nearly 15 percentage points [E39].

Conceded: [E29], [E37], [E39], [E60]. While those headwinds exist, the bear's claim of a fragile margin profile ignores that quarterly operating margins actually expanded to 8% in June 2026 compared to 7% a year prior [E30]. The anxiety over historical peak-to-trough drawdowns [E50] and high positioning near the 52-week range [E5, E45] is decoupled from the reality that the rules-based screen scores the business at a strong 88 out of 100 with a BUY recommendation [E61], backed by explosive TTM sales growth of 67% [E17] and net profit surges of 127% YoY [E64]. Furthermore, the dismissive stance on returns misses that the company's ROCE of 13.27% outperforms the sector benchmark of 10.27% [E10], demonstrating superior capital efficiency. Finally, operational execution is clearly shining through tangible improvements in debtor days from 30.1 down to 17.3 days [E57], generating real free cash flow of Rs 4 Cr [E35] and supporting a conservatively financed balance sheet with a modest debt-to-equity ratio of 0.30x [E36].

Conceded: [E30], [E57], [E35]. The bull's reliance on a single quarter's marginal operating margin uptick to 8% [E30] completely glosses over the severe, structural multi-year compression where operating margins plummeted from 14% to 8% in TTM [E29]. Pointing to an 88/100 screen score [E61] offers little comfort when the underlying stock trades at an inflated P/E of 34.08x against a sector benchmark of 25.59x [E6], an excessive EV/EBITDA of 18.8x [E11], and a rich price-to-book ratio of 5.19x compared to the 2.02x sector norm [E7]. The claim of superior capital efficiency via ROCE [E10] is severely undermined by a low multi-year return on equity of just 10.6% [E60] and a median 5-year ROE of only 10% [E26]. Furthermore, the bull completely ignores that insiders are fleeing, evidenced by a massive promoter stake reduction from 72.47% down to 57.73% [E39], alongside rising borrowings of Rs 21 Cr [E37] and a history of brutal 60.3% drawdowns [E50].
